newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

PT Astra International shares rose sharply on the market yesterday on rumours that founder William Soeryadjaja will buy back into the company. PT Astra manufactures cars in joint ventures with Japanese firms.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard -- on a three-day official visit to Indonesia -- said he was hopeful that trade between the two countries could double to US$10 billion by the year 2000.
State-owned companies PT Telkom and PT Indosat are set to build Indonesia's tallest tower in Jakarta. The tower will be a multimedia centre.
The government is considering revoking the licences of two Indonesian insurance firms PT Maskapai Asuransi Teladan and PT Maskapai Asuransi Timur Besar for failure to submit financial reports.
Indonesia's Surabaya Stock Exchange plans to launch automated remote trading from Thursday following approval by the Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam).
